text:
sqlpipe moves Postgres data to S3 Parquet through three concurrent stages connected by bounded channels.

**Reader** opens a server-side cursor, fetches rows in configurable batches (default 10k), and pushes each batch downstream. Backpressure from a full channel pauses fetches automatically.

**Converter** receives row batches, maps Postgres types to Arrow, and accumulates rows until a row-group threshold (row count or byte size). Completed row groups serialize to Parquet in memory and forward to the uploader.

**Uploader** initiates an S3 multipart upload, streams each Parquet chunk as a part (minimum 5 MB), and completes the upload when the converter signals EOF. Failed parts retry with exponential backoff; after max retries the upload aborts and the pipeline errors.

Channels decouple stage speeds. The reader can outpace the converter briefly; the uploader can lag without blocking row production.
